definition: Grouping time series by shape or dynamics without labels — using elastic distances or learned representations.
details: Grouping time series by shape or dynamics without labels — using elastic distances or learned representations.

explainer.lead: Time series clustering groups series by shape or dynamics without labels. It matters for discovering structure in unlabelled temporal data where no ground-truth categories exist.

tiers.eli5: Nobody tells you the groups in advance; you sort lots of recordings into piles so that ones that move in similar ways end up together.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers group series using elastic distances or learned representations; a pitfall is that the choice of distance or representation shapes the clusters found, and there are no labels to validate against.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, the task partitions a collection of time series into groups by shape or dynamics without labels, using elastic distances or learned representations. No further formal guarantees are specified here.

explainer.example: Unlabelled sensor traces can be sorted into piles by how their curves move over time, without any predefined category names.
